sources.title: Xbox Project Helix is "a console that is also capable of playing games from your PC," says lead dev
sources.text: The Helix is reportedly expected to launch in 2028 Jason Ronald – vice president of Xbox's gaming devices and ecosystem team – has spoken in more detail about what Project Helix actually is. Namely, it doesn't sound like it's a Steam Machine. To celebrate the 25th anniversary since the original Xbox was released and Halo arrived in our lives (and almost 26 since The Rock revealed the console ), Microsoft has released a magazine about the platform online . While a lot of it is about the history of the console, some details about the future of Xbox are sprinkled in there, with news about future releases like Fable, and a hint that there's maybe something going on with games like Crash Bandicoot and Tony Hawk. But the most significant bit of info is some more details about what Project Helix is. Ronald – who Microsoft describes as the vice president of next generation – says "it's really designed to be the ultimate gaming machine – one that removes all the barriers of play that have historically existed," while touting its backwards compatibility capabilities, mentioning that he's "able to bring four generations of my Xbox library and progression with me and have it available instantly." He also speaks about removing "the arbitrary constraints between console and PC games," while explaining more about what Project Helix's rumored PC connection actually is. "We're very clear on the design goal" Ronald explains, "Helix is designed to be a console that is also capable of playing games from your PC. It is not a PC that can also play console games." Of course, the real question is how all-encompassing is the PC integration going to be. Presumably the Xbox Store is a sure bet, and probably Battle.net too. But the idea of having your Steam library available on console would be a pretty unassailable win for the console, but sadly I really don't see that happening in the age of Steam Machines. Xbox Project Helix console could cost as much as $1,800 and is reportedly set to launch by Christmas 2028. sources.name: Kotaku
sources.title: Microsoft Says Of The Next Xbox: ‘Helix Is A Console Capable Of Playing PC Games’
sources.text: Microsoft has put out an online magazine to celebrate 25 years of Xbox , and unquestionably to attempt even more damage control after a gruesome year of studio closures and mass layoffs. Within all the huff and puff lies a surprise: seven pages’ coverage of Project Helix, the codename for the next Xbox console. Within this is revealed the plan for Helix to be able to play games and even progress from every previous Xbox generation, as well as removing “the arbitrary constraints between console and PC games.” So, asks the magazine and indeed us, “is Project Helix a console or a PC?” The answer is very definitively: a console. Sort of. The current generation of consoles were notably described ahead of launch as being far more like PCs in a sealed box than the traditional console designs of yore, and this appears to be something Microsoft is looking to get away from this time out. The emphasis here is on the so-called instantaneous nature of a console. Jason Ronald is Xbox’s VP of “next generation,” and is quoted saying, “When I think about what makes a console magical, it’s that it just makes my games instantly accessible and ready to play in an instant. I don’t have to worry about updating my operating system, updating drivers, configuring different settings.” Which is…a bold claim, given anyone who owns an Xbox will know about having to install the latest updates, waiting for game patches to excruciatingly slowly download without taking advantage of your 1TB ethernet connection, or that unbearable pause each time you load it up for it to fill in the dashboard. But of Project Helix, Ronald says, “it’s really designed to be the ultimate gaming machineâone that removes all the barriers of play that have historically existed. My entire library is accessible to me. I’m able to bring four generations of my Xbox library and progression with me and have it available instantly,” adding, “We’re very clear on the design goal: Helix is designed to be a console that is also capable of playing games from your PC. It is not a PC that can also play console games.” However, it’s hard to know just how clear this distinction is from Ronald’s very next words. “But if you’re a hardcore gamer or a power user who wants to have that deeper level of customizability across settings and performance options, you can absolutely go do it.” So it is a PC then? So confused. Other comments from Ronald include that “We don’t think the next generation is defined by 8K or 240 hertz, or some of the traditional metricsâit’s really about gameplay innovation.” He adds, “It is about leveraging new technical advancements such as neural rendering, to deliver a new level of visual fidelity in more efficient and innovative ways.” Which all rather seems to be laying the ground for a machine that’s not focusing on the very latest and most expensive chipsets, but rather one that’ll take advantage of the more recent progress in upscaling and the like, perhaps to prevent the machine costing an absolute fortune? This topic isn’t ignored. Describing it as a factor “the team couldn’t have foreseen when Project Helix began,” the component crisis gets a mention. “Meeting this challenge has become a primary driver of Helix’s innovation,” says the article. Ronald is quoted once more. “It’s definitely a challenging time, but as a system and a platform designer, it’s also one of the most exciting times because we have to invent entirely new technology to continue to advance the state-of-the-art while also continuing to make things accessible and affordable.” This, he says, is why there’s the focus on neural rendering, adding, “I think you’re going to see more innovation over the next three to five years than you’ve seen in the last 10 years.” It’s all a lot of words to avoid pointing out that Microsoft itself is one of the primary causes of the crisis in the first place, one arm taking all the available components from the other in order to power its AI hubris. Beyond this, the piece delivers some very confusing messaging regarding Xbox’s current desperate rebranding. After a disastrous attempt to call everything from your console to your toaster “an Xbox,” the recent emphasis has been to return to the core idea of the Xbox itself, yet that message gets very lost in Microsoft’s own marketing. We’re told at once that this is all about “the Return of Xboxâthe return of a console,” and then that “Project Helix aims to take a wrecking ball to the dividers currently keeping players and their games apart,” quoting Ronald saying Helix is about “enabling [players] to experience those games wherever they choose to play. It’s about removing barriers to play, removing friction, and those arbitrary boundaries that have existed in the past.” So which is it? There are claims the new UI will adapt to whether the Xbox is being played on the living room TV, or streamed to a mobile device or a PC with mouse and keyboard. This really does sound like a confusion of previous messaging crashing into the current reverse-ferret. There’s no word one when we can expect to see Project Helix in more detail, and certainly nothing on an intended release date. It seems that Microsoft and Sony are currently playing chicken on revealing whether they’re aiming for 2027 or 2028, or perhaps even later given the tumult in the hardware industry. But at least we know it’s a console, not a PC, but also like a PC, and can be streamed to your mobile, or played on PC, and has all of the annoying complexity of PCs taken away, but also still there. sources.title: Xbox Project Helix lead says it's "one of the most exciting times" to be making a new console
sources.text: Xbox is all-in on neural rendering to keep costs down A lead developer on Xbox Project Helix says that rising hardware costs are a primary driver of the upcoming console's development. As part of the console brand's 25th anniversary, Microsoft has released a magazine about Xbox's past, present, and future . This online magazine includes an interview with Jason Ronald, vice president of next-generation console development at Microsoft and the lead for Project Helix. In this interview, he clarifies that Xbox Project Helix is "a console that is also capable of playing games from your PC," rather than the other way around. Obviously, the biggest conversations about the Xbox Project Helix – and the PS6 – are cost. Hardware prices are rising thanks to the ongoing global RAM shortages brought on by AI companies who just need to let your weird uncle generate what he looks like as a Simpson to post on Facebook. The Xbox Series X|S , PS5 , and Nintendo Switch 2 have all had price increases over the past year, but Ronald says keeping the price down is a crucial motivator in the console's design. "It's definitely a challenging time," Ronald says, adding, "it’s also one of the most exciting times, because we have to invent entirely new technology to continue to advance the state-of-the-art while also continuing to make things accessible and affordable." He explains the cost factor is why the team behind Project Helix is "really focused on advancements like neural rendering, because it’s an entirely new way to generate a frame without requiring more computational horsepower, additional memory, and things like that." Obviously AI-assisted tech was a big talking point within games before the memory crisis, but it feels like it's only going to become more prominent. Sony has been implementing QSSR frame generation tech into its PS5 games , likely in part because nobody can afford a PS5 Pro now that it's almost $1,000. And with things going like they are, it's probably going to be the norm heading forward… let's just hope Xbox puts its money where its mouth is and actually makes the Helix affordable. But given the current rumor is it's going to be $1,800, I'm not too hopeful. sources.title: The next Xbox, Project Helix, is a console and "not a PC" says Microsoft, as it clarifies that computational power isn't sole focus this time
sources.text: "It is about leveraging new technical advancements such as neural rendering." Microsoft has stressed that its next-generation Xbox console, Project Helix, "is not a PC that can also play console games", but rather "a console that is also capable of playing games from your PC". The company has also underlined the importance of using gen-AI-adjacent "neural rendering" technology going forwards, and a desire to remove "all the barriers of play that have historically existed" - notably in making the past generations of games playable. The details come from a Microsoft-produced Xbox magazine made available digitally yesterday , and a Helix-related feature speaking to Xbox vice president of next generation, Jason Ronald. "When we think about Project Helix, it's really designed to be the ultimate gaming machine," Ronald said, "one that removes all the barriers of play that have historically existed. My entire library is accessible to me. I'm able to bring four generations of my Xbox library and progression with me and have it available instantly. And we remove the arbitrary constraints between console and PC games. "We're very clear on the design goal," Ronald later added. "Helix is designed to be a console that is also capable of playing games from your PC. It is not a PC that can also play console games. The goal is making it easy, intuitive, and instant to access my games. But if you're a hardcore gamer or a power user who wants to have that deeper level of customisability across settings and performance options, you can absolutely go do it." Notably, Ronald seemed to suggest that Helix - the console, not the handheld; "Helix" refers to a couple of machines - isn't solely focused on computational grunt. Indeed, he said the next generation wasn't about hitting 8K resolutions and 240 hertz frame-rates, but instead leaning on technologies like "neural rendering" - i.e. generative-AI - and encouraging innovation. "It's about deeper immersion," Ronald said. "It is about leveraging new technical advancements such as neural rendering to deliver a new level of visual fidelity in more efficient and innovative ways. It's about new kinds of games and new game experiences that we haven't been able to do before. What excites me about the future is the idea of entirely new types of games that have never been possible before, delivered through all the innovation in the silicon and the hardware and the platform that we're delivering." While referencing the global component shortage and exorbitant prices of computer hardware, he added: "This is a big reason why we're really focused on advancements like neural rendering because it's an entirely new way to generate a frame without requiring more computational horsepower, additional memory, and things like that. I think you're going to see more innovation over the next three to five years than you've seen in the last 10 years." Xbox boss Asha Sharma also recently talked up the importance of generative-AI-sounding technology in Xbox's future , saying "too many ideas never become games", and that "a single person will soon be able to wield capabilities that once required entire nations". Another key part of Xbox's Helix vision is compatibility and game preservation. "Game preservation is core to Xbox," Ronald went as far as to say. "Not only do we feel like it's the right thing for the industry, we feel a deep responsibility as one of its biggest platforms and publishers. For the first 30 years of game development, nobody really thought about game preservation when they were designing their hardware, when they were building their games." Xbox is apparently working with game-makers to ensure games can not only be played now but also 20 to 30 years into the future. The other key facet of Microsoft's push the familiar Play Anywhere mantra, whereby one game can be played across multiple devices, maintaining your game-progress as you go. This is fundamental to Microsoft's handheld-and-console Helix plan, and something we've seen the company dry-run with the Xbox ROG Ally X handheld . "It's this notion that not only does my library move with me, but my progress moves with me as well," Ronald said. "Because I fully expect that when I'm in the middle of an 80-hour RPG, if I'm 25 hours into that and I want to play it on another device, I should be able to instantly resume from where I was. Those are things that today are becoming more common, but I think in the future it's going to be a baseline expectation of all players." Ronald wouldn't be drawn on the issue of price regarding Project Helix - a recent report suggested Helix could be priced up to $1800 - referring to it only as both "a challenging time" but an "exciting one", because "we have to invent entirely new technology to continue to advance the state-of-the-art while also continuing to make things accessible and affordable". Ronald also wouldn't reference a release date, though the report referenced above suggested the handheld Helix machine will release next holiday, 2027, and the console Helix machine the year after. The next generation, then, seems to be around the corner.

sources.title: Xbox afirma que Project Helix é um console capaz de rodar jogos de PC — e não o contrário
sources.text: A Microsoft divulgou novos detalhes sobre o Project Helix, seu console de nova geração, e reforçou a ideia de que o videogame é capaz de rodar jogos de PC — mas não um PC que consegue rodar jogos de console. Em entrevista publicada na revista especial de 25 anos do Xbox, Jason Ronald, vice-presidente da próxima geração da marca, explicou que o projeto foi desenvolvido para funcionar como um console tradicional, e não como um computador com recursos de videogame. “O Helix foi projetado para ser um console capaz também de rodar jogos do seu PC. Não é um PC que também roda jogos de console”, afirmou Ronald. O executivo também destacou que o aparelho pretende eliminar barreiras entre as bibliotecas de jogos de PC e Xbox, na intenção de manter a experiência simples e intuitiva para os jogadores. Segundo Ronald, a proposta do Project Helix é reunir diferentes bibliotecas em um único dispositivo e permitir com que os jogadores acessem seus títulos com mais facilidade. O console também deve oferecer compatibilidade com quatro gerações de jogos e preservar o progresso das contas Xbox. O executivo explicou que a experiência poderá ser adaptada a diferentes perfis de jogadores. Quem preferir uma experiência tradicional terá acesso rápido aos jogos, enquanto usuários mais avançados poderão personalizar configurações e opções de desempenho. “Quando penso no que torna um console mágico, é o fato de ele tornar meus jogos instantaneamente acessíveis e prontos para jogar”, afirmou Ronald. Ele também destacou que os jogadores não precisarão se preocupar com atualizações de drivers ou configurações típicas de um PC. A ideia, segundo o executivo, é criar uma plataforma que reúna a praticidade dos consoles com a flexibilidade dos computadores. “Quando pensamos no Project Helix, ele foi realmente concebido para ser a máquina de jogos definitiva — uma que remove todas as barreiras de jogo que existiram historicamente”, declarou. Durante a entrevista, Ronald também comentou sobre os desafios de desenvolver um novo console em meio à crise de componentes de PC. Segundo ele, a Microsoft está investindo em tecnologias como a renderização neural para melhorar o desempenho sem exigir mais poder computacional ou memória. “É definitivamente um momento desafiador, mas, como designer de sistemas e plataformas, também é um dos momentos mais empolgantes”, afirmou. O executivo explicou que a equipe busca novas soluções para avançar tecnologicamente e, ao mesmo tempo, manter os custos de produção e os preços sustentáveis. Ronald citou a renderização neural como uma das principais apostas para a próxima geração. A tecnologia pode abranger diferentes técnicas de processamento de imagem, como aprimoramento de resolução, geração de quadros e reconstrução de iluminação, embora a Microsoft ainda não tenha detalhado como pretende aplicá-la no Project Helix. O executivo também afirmou que a próxima geração não deve ser definida apenas por especificações tradicionais — como resolução 8K ou taxas de atualização de 240 Hz. Para ele, o foco estará em novas experiências de jogo, maior imersão e avanços visuais mais eficientes. E você, está ansioso para conhecer a próxima geração de consoles? stories.title: Grand Theft Auto VI Limited-Edition PS5 DualSense Controllers Are Out This Week
stories.summary: Preorders are live for Grand Theft Auto VI Limited-Edition PS5 DualSense Controllers, but stock is limited. Hurry if you want one.

sources.name: IGN
sources.title: Grand Theft Auto VI Limited-Edition PS5 DualSense Controllers Are Out This Week
sources.text: GTA 6 the game is almost here, and so are the PS5 controllers. Sony and Rockstar are partnering up to release two different limited-edition GTA 6-themed PS5 DualSense controllers. One is black and one is white. The designs are relatively subtle, but they both look tasteful and appealing. They cost $84.99 each and are set to release on November 19, the same day as the game. Preorders are live now ( see at Walmart ). Read on for more info. The white version of the controller is available in limited quantities at a variety of retailers. Sony says the white one “embodies Vice City at daybreak, from its white sands and pastel skies to all its laid-back glamour.” If black is more your speed, you can get the black color varaiant. The black version is exclusive to PlayStation Direct . Sony says this one “captures the energy of Vice City’s iconic nightlife.” On both controllers, the inside of the grips have a “shimmering, color-shifting finish” that changes color as you turn the controllers in the light. Both feature a big but subtle “VI” on the touchpad, as well as textured, inset palm tree etchings in the grips. Aside from that, these are your standard DualSense controllers with all of the expected functionality: haptic feedback, adaptive triggers, a big old touch pad – the usual good stuff we all appreciate. In other news, you can preorder Grand Theft Auto VI for PS5 ahead of the November 19 launch. If you do preorder, whether in physical or digital format , you’ll be able to preload it a week ahead of launch so you’re not taking up precious time downloading when you could be playing. “Physical” copies don’t include a disk — just a download code — but they're already shipping, so you'll still have time to preload. In the meantime, you can rewatch the GTA 6 extended look as many times as you want. If you're in the market for other PS5 controllers, the Marvel's Wolverine DualSense looks pretty great as well. Chris Reed is a senior commerce editor and deals expert for IGN. He also runs IGN's LEGO coverage and maintains the upcoming release dates articles for video games , LEGO sets , and 4K Blu-rays . You can follow him on Bluesky .

sources.title: Gangland Tales From the Frontline of Rockstar's Real-Life Grand Theft Auto Research
sources.text: Gregory Johnson was sitting in the back of a police car, but he wasn’t under arrest. In fact, the cops were just as nervous as him. Johnson, an experienced researcher for Rockstar, was scouting the underbelly of Los Angeles for Grand Theft Auto 5, an open-world crime game set in a fictionalized L.A. called Los Santos, which is Spanish for “The Saints.” Outside the car window, there were no saints to be found. “We were doing a ride along in East L.A., very late at night,” Johnson told IGN in a recent interview. “It's still an active gang neighborhood where stuff is going down, so I'm knowing all the signs and seeing a lot of it, and I was super nervous about it. I was like, ‘We're probably okay, but what if we're not?’” As the car pulled a corner, a whistle cried out from a nearby rooftop. Another series of whistles quickly followed, fading as they moved along a human daisy chain — an alarm system from a series of rooftop sentries to warn other gang members cops were on the prowl. With that, a couple of bikes shot down alleyways, pedalling fast to catch up before pulling up either side of the car to escort it on its patrol through the neighbourhood. The riders stared into the windows through masks. “The Mexican gangs of Los Angeles are known to be very organized,” Johnson explained. “And I quickly got to the point where I was like, I know we've got police with us. I know they're armed. The logic of the moment holds that nobody wants this to turn into any situation. They don't want to generally initiate violence with the police. We don't want violence. We're just here to get a feel for the place and maybe poke our long lenses out of the windows and shoot some pictures. “So we just got through it and ran our routes, and got everybody back to the hotel safely, but once I saw the neighborhood activate… I mean, it's amazing to see if you're going to try and duplicate it with the gameplay, right? But when you're actually in it, you're like, ‘This could go bad.’” Even that feeling is important — the dread, the worry that things could boil over at any moment — when trying to capture the essence of a city, from its decadent hilltop houses in the Hollywood Hills to its low-income neighbourhoods over the Los Angeles River. Mood is a hard thing to capture unless you’ve felt the electricity in the air yourself as fight or flight kicks in and the hairs on the back of your neck stand to attention. “I had to keep everybody cool in the group,” Johnson, a Floridian who lived most of his life in New York, remembered. “We've got a bunch of guys from Scotland and England, Ireland. Never seen anything like it. They're like, ‘Is everything okay, Greg?’ ‘Yeah, everything's fine.’ Completely lying. ‘Everything's fine, guys.’ It was somewhere between location scouting and espionage.” Johnson himself knew the streets fairly well already, but he was partly recruited not just because of what he knew, but because of who he knew. Having worked on hip-hop’s Vibe Magazine for 16 years, as well as other prestigious music mags like Source, he was already embedded in the culture. He knew the people in the music industry Rockstar was working with, and helped make introductions where he could. He had his finger pushed hard into the pulse of an ever-shifting culture. “Dan Houser had a vision for a professional research team that could easily deliver academic information,” Johnson explained. “Basically an internal form of reporting, cultural research. The role grew right as we established the department, but he had tried to get together various versions of it, and when he hired me and a couple other people around that time, I had an academic background as well as a background in hip hop journalism, and I knew the culture inside and out. We would go through tons of pop culture and various applicable subcultures. “Rockstar has represented Jamaican yardies extremely well. The mafia culture in GTA, the Yakuza culture in GTA — all of these different subcultures and themes were really rich targets for deep dives. The better the graphics got, the better the gameplay got, the better the voiceovers got — the ambient stuff, the missions — the more background information was required to distill it into these memorable, immersive gameplay experiences. We did real life research, and these broad surveys of popular culture and the popular imagination, depending on the setting of the game, the timing of the game, and the artistic and creative direction.” In his job as a researcher, Johnson brought a boots-on-the-ground style of journalism to the research trips, embedding himself in various cultures, from gangs to underground street racing meets. He was a voyeur, one of Rockstar’s documentarians, turning moves on the street into weekly reports for the internal blog, keeping plugged into whatever city the company was making a fictional recreation of, and distilling all of that into stories the writers could use as jumping off points. Some don’t make it into the games, but others showed up as radio advertisements, pretend TV shows, full character arcs, random encounters, ambient NPC chatter, and more. They found interesting characters and used parts of their personalities and personal stories to ground GTA’s fictional players in some form of truth. At one point, a smuggler came across Rockstar’s radar. This was a guy who knew the late drug lord Pablo Escobar personally and was a major player in the Cocaine Cowboys era, the Scarface days, when the Medellin Cartel trafficked white powder into Miami through the ‘70s and ‘80s. According to Johnson, some of the interviews with the smuggler likely informed the Cayo Perico heist in GTA Online. “This was one of the guys that helped the Colombians figure out their underwater submersible system, where they were, with submarines of various quality, able to bring stuff from the Colombian coast into the U.S.,” Johnson said. “That later changed. sources.title: The History of Grand Theft Auto Easter Eggs
sources.text: When you’ve got an open world as big and dense as Grand Theft Auto, you’ve got to fill it with something. Restaurants, tennis courts, hidden packages, Strangers and Freaks. All kinds of treats to reward our exploration, some buried deeper than others. From hearts and minds to signs and shrines, the inside jokes and little secrets Rockstar’s calling card tucked in every corner of the map. This is the history of Grand Theft Auto easter eggs. The top-down Grand Theft Autos are too sparse and pixelated for the kind of buried treasures that would await us in the 3D era, but easter eggs exist even in this perspective. The most famous secret of the first GTA games involves lines of chanting bald NPCs dressed in orange robes, evocative of the Hare Krishna devotees famous for descending upon travelers at airports. If you can run the entire procession down sequentially, you’re rewarded with a seemingly nonsensical shout of “GOURANGA!” The phrase, a Krishna term meaning “be happy,” became the series’ signature meme among the early fanbase and resurfaced in the first few sequels, with hidden bonuses for mowing down Elvis impersonators in GTA 2 and football hooligans in GTA: London. For a series so devoted to examining the American dream, it’s easy to forget that Grand Theft Auto is British-born. The Scottish studio that created the series and the English brothers who made it a phenomenon belong to a storied Britdev tradition of taking the mick in the margins. From the ZX Spectrum emulator Rare buried in GoldenEye to Team17’s profane cheat codes and salty rants against Amiga Power magazine, British studios excel at hiding cheeky winks within their games. DMA Design, later Rockstar North, is no exception. DMA logos are disguised among the scenery, the pager randomly rags on staffers, and director Keith Hamilton himself sends you on a mission to find “the elements of GTA.” You can unlock R-rated language by naming your character after the studio’s credited “Project Bloke.” The developers are sharing their private jokes with the players, leaving their signatures in out-of-reach places. It’s been that way since the very first easter egg: The people in the game are talking to us, but they make it hard to hear them. The developers are very present in GTA 3. The game came in hot, suffered hurried changes, and still showed a lot of its arcadey roots. The veil between the game and its inner workings is thinnest here, you can out of bounds and fly the unflyable dodo across nonexistent towns named after team members. Look to La Luna through the eyes of a sniper rifle and pull the trigger to change the size of the moon, since the devs never decided how big it should be. You had to be willing to break the game a little bit to earn your peek behind the curtain, but it wasn’t that hard to do in 2001. Rockstar anticipated our escape. If you drive up a staircase near a parking lot in Staunton Island, you can hop out and use your car to climb onto a normally inaccessible roof. A precision jump drops you in an unused back alley, where you’ll find a sign that says “You weren’t supposed to be able to get here, you know.” The devs mercifully included a ramp to get us back into the game proper rather than risking a softlock. They knew we’d be snooping around. Some developers would dummy out this kind of content once it's discovered, but Rockstar maintained it as a running gag, slapping messages in hard-to-find spots throughout the series. In GTA: Vice City, Tommy can clip through a wall near the VCN helipad to enter a room with a simple marvel pedestal, upon which rests a single egg emblazoned “Happy Easter!” You’ll find no such ovoid in GTA: San Andreas. The closest you’ll come is the Gant Bridge that connects San Fierro with Las Venturas. The visitor center below contains a display serving up fun facts about the bridge. On closer inspection the text is actually information on the structure’s internal game files, like how it’s made up of 16,000 polygons and takes up a “staggering 1.27mb of disc space.” The sign was actually updated by Grove Street Games for the Definitive Edition release. After 17 years, the bridge’s triangle count doubled, the textures increased fourfold, and the disk space increased a whopping 3,000 percent. Good thing storage has stayed so affordable! If CJ can tear himself away from the field trip exhibits and land himself on top of the southern suspension tower, he’ll find another secret scolding among the orange steel rivets: “There are no Easter Eggs up here. Go away.” Clearly anticipating you’d be crushed by the disappointment of your futile search, Rockstar eases the pain with a handy parachute to get you back on your feet. Grand Theft Auto 4 does the bit, too. And cleverly, though nothing mind-blowing for the most part. A museum placard giving out about how hard the dinosaur skeletons were to sculpt, or a warning inside of the Statue of Happiness, through a door in the base reached only by air. “No hidden content,” reads an engraving by a collision-free closed door. Walk through the illusory wall, however and you’ll encounter something far more visceral than anything that’s come before. Inside you’ll find a ladder vanishing upwards into the body of the rusted copper colossus. Reach the top and you’ll find a scaffold standing just below a huge and hideous heart. Suspended painfully from chains, its maddening beat thunders inside the internal steel chamber and it cannot die. You’re not going to fit this thing in a bunny’s basket. It’s a darker, more unsettling easter egg than any that’s come before, even if it’s apparently just a jab at Hillary Clinton, who had gone after Rockstar hard as a senator during the San Andreas Hot Coffee scandal. The Heart of Liberty City is the stuff that creepypastas are made of, legends spread in schoolyards and over IRC. The series had outgrown this style of secret by the time of GTA 5. The mysterious content within its sprawling map goes far beyond the scope of eas

sources.title: GTA 6 streaming restrictions in China apparently don't allow any grand theft auto
sources.text: Or violence, or most forms of debauchery, really GTA 6 's apparent streaming rules in China effectively turn the game into a sightseeing simulator, and presumably severely restrict story playthroughs. Despite GTA 6 not actually releasing in mainland China – with many likely to import the game's Hong Kong release – Yahoo Taiwan reports (via machine translation) that Douyin (Mainland China and Hong Kong's version of TikTok) has acquired the rights to stream GTA 6 in China. This seems to have coincided with Rockstar opening a Douyin account to advertise pre-loading for the game on the platform. However, this was followed by TikTok reportedly releasing a series of guidelines for anyone keen to stream the game. While the guidelines were not released to the public, a TikTok creator has apparently revealed them by sharing a URL from a domain owned by Douyin and TikTok creator ByteDance. However, access to the document was reportedly disabled once reports about its content emerged. Obviously, GTA is known for its violence, drugs, sex, and all flavors of debauchery the player can partake in as part of its open world. But these supposed guidelines apparently prohibit players from livestreaming aspects of the game like stealing cars (grand theft auto, if you will), attacking civilians, using emojis, wearing revealing clothing, and fighting police officers. On top of that, it's requested that players black out the screen or adjust its color to avoid showing bloodshed. A reportedly leaked part of the document shows similar color-changing being used for Resident Evil Requiem . Obviously, this has been somewhat clowned on, as without all of that, what does GTA 6 have left? With people reportedly joking that it turns the game into a good morals simulator while questioning whether any of the story will even be playable under these restrictions, given that Lucia and Jason are seemingly in constant conflict with the police. That being said, Rockstar has said that GTA 6 will "provide mechanisms that encourage" empathy in the game, so perhaps it won't be too far off for some people's playthroughs. But hey, at least that version of the game will be welcome to some people . sources.title: Grand Theft Auto 6 hacker pleads guilty to all charges
sources.text: Arion Kurtaj released dozens of GTA 6 videos to the public more than a year before the game was formally revealed. The BBC reports that Arion Kurtaj, who hacked Rockstar and dumped a massive trove of content from Grand Theft Auto 6 more than a year before it was formally revealed, has pleaded guilty to that and other hacks carried out while he was a member of the Lapsus$ hacking group. Kurtaj's hack of Rockstar was notable not for the GTA 6 infodump that followed, but because of how it was carried out: With an Amazon Fire Stick , a mobile phone, and a Bluetooth keyboard and mouse, connected to a TV in a Travelodge hotel room where he was being held under police protection because of threats against him made by rival hackers over stolen bitcoin. A 2023 assessment found Kurtaj had "acute autism" and was determined to return to "cybercrime" as soon as possible, despite the fact that he was literally standing trial for doing cybercrimes. Because of that, the jury was asked to determine if he had committed the hacks (it found he had) but not whether he had done so with criminal intent; he was subsequently sentenced to an indefinite stay at a secure hospital , where he would remain unless and until doctors determined that he was no longer a danger. As we noted at the time, "danger" might seem a bit of a strong word for someone who leaked videogame footage, but the Lapsus$ group had also hacked Microsoft , Samsung , Nvidia and UK telecom company BT&EE, and stole millions in cryptocurrency from individuals. Kurtaj was also reportedly violent while in hospital custody, causing "dozens" of reports of injuries or property damage. In July 2026, that 'no longer a danger' determination was presumably made, as Kurtaj was released from hospital and moved to prison to await retrial. He has now pleaded guilty to multiple hacks carried out when he was 16 and 17 years old, including the Rockstar hack that led to the GTA 6 leak. He also pleaded guilty to assaults on workers while in custody, which the BBC report says included "multiple biting incidents." As I said when Kurtaj was moved from hospital to prison, the whole thing strikes me as odd. The big question is how Kurtaj's state of mind at the time of the crimes will influence the outcome of his guilty plea, given that a previous court determined that he needed multiple years of institutionalization. BBC tech reporter Joe Tidy, who's been following the case since Kurtaj's transfer, also described it as "an unusual move" in his report. Coincidentially, one must assume, Grand Theft Auto 6 launches for consoles on November 19. Kurtaj will be sentenced at a future date. The leaker who goes by Cyberleek , who recently distributed several GTA 6 gameplay videos apparently taken with a development build of the game, remains at large. From there he graduated to the glory days of Sierra Online adventures and Microprose sims, ran a local BBS, learned how to build PCs, and developed a longstanding love of RPGs, immersive sims, and shooters. He began writing videogame news in 2007 for The Escapist and somehow managed to avoid getting fired until 2014, when he joined the storied ranks of PC Gamer. He covers all aspects of the industry, from new game announcements and patch notes to legal disputes, Twitch beefs, esports, and Henry Cavill. Lots of Henry Cavill. sources.title: Ghost of Yotei Drops to £28 in PlayStation’s UK Black Friday Sale
sources.text: PlayStation has kicked off its Black Friday 2026 with a whole raft of deals in the UK this week. Among the best of those is the deal to pick up Ghost of Yotei for £28 from Amazon, down from its RRP of £54.99. This is the best price we've found across UK retailers. If you're after the complete edition (including the DLC), it's also down to £39.99 at Smyths . If you haven’t picked up a copy of this game yet, the Black Friday sales season could be your best chance at this excellent price. Just one caveat to make you aware of: this deal is only available on the physical copy of the game, so if you’re hoping to pick it up on the PlayStation Store at the same price, you won’t be able to. We gave this game an 8/10 , praising its stunning visuals and new lead character, Atsu. Set in 1603 in Ezo (modern-day Hokkaido), the story follows Atsu, a mercenary on a quest for vengeance against a group of outlaws known as the “Yōtei Six” who brutally murdered her family 16 years prior to the events of the game. The game is completely standalone, taking place 300 years after Ghost of Tsushima and featuring a whole new cast of characters and set in a different location. So if you never got round to playing Ghost of Tsushima, rest assured that you don’t need to play it first before you give into Ghost of Yōtei. Our reviewer, Michael Higham, said this about this game: “Sequels are opportunities to either build upon a predecessor and push boundaries, or refine what was already great and deliver that again with a stronger focus. With Ghost of Yotei, developer Sucker Punch leaned heavily into the latter approach, and the result is more captivating open-world action and unbelievably striking visuals at every turn. It doesn't try to revolutionize things, sticking pretty close to 2020's Ghost of Tsushima in general, but I don’t necessarily mind when that means it can expand in aspects that matter and offer a tighter distillation of the samurai fantasy that was originally promised. Not many games in recent memory can hang their hat on having combat as fluid and satisfying as this, and it's packed into a revenge tale that makes for a more human story.” The savings in PlayStation goodies don’t end with this deal. DualSense controllers are £20 off, as are physical copies of Marvel’s Wolverine. You can also get £90 off a PlayStation VR2, and, to top it all off, PlayStation Plus subscribers can get an additional 5% off accessories purchased directly through PlayStation, on top of the standard promotional discounts. That’s right, we’ve got deals on top of deals. You can keep track of all the best PlayStation deals here over the Black Friday period . sources.title: Star Wars: Galactic Racer is getting much-requested split-screen multiplayer and new mode in 2027
sources.text: The surprisingly awesome arcade podracing game Star Wars: Galactic Racer is getting split-screen multiplayer next year after loud fan requests, developer Fuse Games has announced. Split-screen racing comes as part of an entirely new mode called Free Play that'll also allow players to mix and match vehicles, characters, tracks and planets in a galaxy far, far away. So, maybe don't expect to bring friends into the game's vast, pre-existing suite of modes just yet. "We heard you," the studio wrote on social media. "Local split-screen multiplayer racing is coming in early 2027. A dedicated team at Fuse Games has been working hard to bring a brand new mode, Free Play, to Star Wars: Galactic Racer. This new mode will allow you to choose your vehicle, character, planet, and race track to race alone or with up to 3 other players in local split-screen action." We’ve heard you! Local split-screen multiplayer racing is coming in early 2027. A dedicated team at @Fuse_Games has been working hard to bring a brand new mode, Free Play, to STAR WARS: Galactic Racer™. This new mode will allow you to choose your vehicle, character, planet, and race track to race alone or with up to 3 other players in local split-screen action. Galactic Racer already has a pretty good selection of online multiplayer modes, like the 12-player speeder races and 8-player podracing tours, but there's currently no way to play with your mates in the same room. Chris Donlan loved the thrilling racing game for mixing the best bits of Star Wars and Burnout - Fuse Games does have plenty of old Criterion DNA, mind you. "It's new games, with Roguelite choices and endless unlockables, and it's also old games, with cruel and ingenious courses where everything can be lost in an instant. It's a Galaxy Far, Far Away, and it's also Paradise City," he wrote in Eurogamer's five-star review . With Galactic Racer and Zero Company under its belt, Lucasfilm Games said it's now "more flexible" about which developers it accepts pitches from . Hopefully, that'll lead to even more interesting games set in Star Wars' ultra flexible world.

sources.name: Polygon
sources.title: Star Wars: Galactic Racer Officially Getting the Feature Every Racing Game Needs
sources.text: The year's best Star Wars game gets even better Scrib doon! Star Wars: Galactic Racer developer Fuse Games announced the racing sim is getting a key ingredient next year: split-screen multiplayer. Up to four players will be able to square off on the same screen at once after the update. "We’ve heard you!" Fuse's social media announcement begins, as the developer acknowledges this is a feature players have wanted since the game launched in early October. "A dedicated team at Fuse Games has been working hard to develop a new mode: Free Play. Choose your vehicle, character, planet, and track to race alone or with up to 3 other players in local splitscreen action." Galactic Racer launched with multiplayer modes, but they're only playable online. It's not clear if local split-screen multiplayer will also be playable in those other modes, like Podracing Tour, or if you'll only be able to enjoy split-screen gameplay in the new Free Play mode. Star Wars fans have eaten well this year. Bit Reactor's Star Wars Zero Company brought turn-based tactical gameplay to the Clone Wars a month and a half before Galactic Racer let everyone join the Outer Rim's Galactic League. It's one of the year's highest-rated games , and don't be surprised if Galactic Racer takes home some hardware come awards season . "The game's learning curve is steep, and there's a lot to manage and think about in a race. But boy, when you get there, the rush is unmatched. This is a game of both blistering speed and tactical nuance, where smart use of your abilities is just as important as racing reflexes. It's a deep game system, and the further you get into a run, the better and more rewarding it gets," Polygon's Oli Welsh wrote in his Galactic Racer review , where he called it "the best arcade racing game in a generation." Star Wars: Galactic Racer is available on PlayStation 5, Windows PC, and Xbox Series X. The Free Play mode will be added "in early 2027," according to Fuse Games' announcement.

sources.name: GamesRadar
sources.title: Star Wars: Fate of the Old Republic director was "circling" a revival of BioWare's KOTOR for years
sources.text: "What if we put a dent in the universe and made, essentially, the next in the line of Knights of the Old Republic games?" I imagine most BioWare fans would argue that the studio's peak happened somewhere between Dragon Age: Origins and Mass Effect 2. For me, though, the absolute high point was Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic, and I was always a little bitter that the devs moved on to create Mass Effect rather than finishing Revan's story in a proper KOTOR 3. That's why seeing Casey Hudson, original director of KOTOR, return with a spiritual successor in Star Wars: Fate of the Old Republic is so exciting, and it's apparently been a long time coming. "It is really a dream project for us," Hudson says in an interview with The Fourth Curtain podcast . After leaving BioWare – for a second time – in 2020, he founded a new studio called Humanoid Origin, which was developing a "sci-fi action RPG" that would've been a "brand-new IP." That studio shuttered in 2024 after an "unexpected shortfall of funding," leaving Hudson to figure out what to do next. "We had lots of ideas, including, like, 'Do we get funding to continue with what we were doing? Are there other paths forward?' But over the years – myself and folks from our team, we worked on the original Knights of the Old Republic way back in the day, and since then BioWare also had the Old Republic MMO. So we've kept up connections with folks at Lucasfilm ," he says. Some time after Humanoid Origin shut down, Hudson explains, "the head of Disney Games reached out and said, 'Hey, what if we put a dent in the universe and made, essentially, the next in the line of Knights of the Old Republic games? The spiritual successor.'" Hudson says he'd been "circling" the idea of returning to KOTOR for some time. "It's something that I would love to do, but I was either doing other things or other projects. There were times when maybe it wasn't right for Lucasfilm, or they weren't ready for it. There wasn't really a fit." He was excited both by the possibility of returning to KOTOR and bringing back "some of the the top folks we've worked with," but surviving a studio shutdown leads you to "become the most skeptical person on earth," he says. "You don't really trust anyone to follow through with a deal or funding until things are signed, done, and legit." Getting those contracts finalized is how Hudson spent "the first half" of 2025. Then he spent the rest of the year "just starting to assemble our team, doing a prototype, and then creating the announcement trailer." Weekly digests, tales from the communities you love, and more Yes, that means that Fate of the Old Republic had only barely entered development at the time of its reveal at The Game Awards last year, but Hudson seems confident we won't be waiting forever for it to be finished. The team works "at a very brisk pace," and he says we should expect "new announcements" sometime next year. Star Wars: Fate of the Old Republic could be going for "a more simple hero's journey" to avoid BioWare's "self-indulgent" storytelling, says ex-Dragon Age boss Dustin Bailey joined the GamesRadar team as a Staff Writer in May 2022, and is currently based in Missouri. He's been covering games (with occasional dalliances in the worlds of anime and pro wrestling) since 2015, first as a freelancer, then as a news writer at PCGamesN for nearly five years. His love for games was sparked somewhere between Metal Gear Solid 2 and Knights of the Old Republic, and these days you can usually find him splitting his entertainment time between retro gaming, the latest big action-adventure title, or a long haul in American Truck Simulator. Jason and Lucia have always known the deck is stacked against them. But when an easy score goes wrong, they find themselves on the darkest side of the sunniest place in America, in the middle of a criminal conspiracy stretching across the state of Leonida — forced to rely on each other more than ever if they want to make it out alive. Purchase prior to 19 November 2026 23:59:59 to receive The Vintage Vice City Pack and one month of GTA+. Grand Theft Auto VI is coming to XBOX Cloud Gaming at launch! Ranger’s Path: National Park Simulator – November 17 XBOX Play Anywhere In Ranger’s Path: National Park Simulator , you take on the everyday responsibilities of a real park ranger in the stunning Faremont National Park. Restore and maintain scenic trails, assist visitors, and document wildlife in a living, breathing ecosystem. You’ll clear blocked paths, collect litter, fix broken signs – and occasionally drop everything to respond to urgent wildlife sightings or missing hikers. Each day brings new tasks and surprises. Unicorn Academy: Island of Magic – November 17 Smart Delivery You are invited to join Unicorn Academy! Create a magical connection with your own unicorn and bond with Sophia, Ava, Layla and the other heroes from the series. Step into the magical world of Unicorn Academy and begin your very own adventure! Create your own first-year student at the academy and call upon the help of Unicorn Academy’s favorite characters. Groom, race and bond with your unicorn. Embark on missions to stop Ravenzella’s evil plot. Dark Rail – November 18 XBOX Play Anywhere Turn-based management roguelike. Command the Inquisition and rule an industrial city on the empire’s edge. Use your train to meet prisoner shipment quotas by hunting heretics and slaying magical beasts. Produce supplies, contain revolt, and sacrifice prisoners to stop the madness. Vice: Magic City Mayhem is a top-down 8-bit retro action/adventure game inspired by Zelda with a Vice City theme. Step into the shoes of Dutch, one of Magic City’s most feared enforcers, on a thrilling and dangerous quest to rescue your one true love, Sophie. Navigate through the chaos of wild nightclubs, scenic beaches, and raptor-infested yachts in this raunchy, high-stakes adventure. Time Machine: Hidden Objects – November 19 XBOX Play Anywhere Are you brave enough to step inside a time machine and rewrite history? Welcome to a captivating hidden object adventure that takes you on an unforgettable journey through space and time. Join young scientist Herbert Fink as he faces difficult yet fascinating challenges that will test your wits. What starts as an ordinary trip out of town quickly transforms into a thrilling sci-fi detective investigation, full of deep intrigue and mysterious temporal anomalies. Cats in Wonderland – November 20 Smart Delivery / XBOX Play Anywhere The Queen of Hearts had a fit of rage after the Cheshire Cat refused to be her pet and ordered the capture of all the cats in Wonderland. Find them before her and prevent anything bad from happening. Cats in Wonderland is a hidden object game where you need to find all the hidden cats in Wonderland. Explore the maps, find items to access new areas, and gather the resistance to defeat the Queen of Hearts. Dig deep, descend fast, and survive the darkness! DRILL DRILL DRILL is a pixel art cave-diving adventure where every floor brings new dangers, precious crystals, and a giant statue that wants to eat the very well you’re trying to escape through. Players will need to carefully plan their route and help the followers climb, jump over dangerous areas, and reach their destination. It’s fast. It’s fun. It’s addicting. sources.title: GTA 6 chega nesta semana! TecMundo terá lives diárias até a Black Friday com o game
sources.text: A chegada de Grand Theft Auto VI (GTA 6) está cada vez mais próxima e promete movimentar a indústria dos games. O game estreia oficialmente em 19 de novembro no PS5 e Xbox Series S/X, e nós vamos entrar com tudo no clima de Vice City. Para acompanhar um dos lançamentos mais aguardados de todos os tempos, o TecMundo e o VOXL realizarão uma maratona de transmissões ao vivo com o título da Rockstar Games. As lives começam no dia 18 de novembro e seguem diariamente até a Black Friday, em 27 de novembro. A programação terá início às 10h (horário de Brasília) de quarta-feira, 18 de novembro, com transmissões de aproximadamente 10 horas por dia. A ideia é acompanhar de perto a chegada do novo jogo da Rockstar Games, explorar suas novidades e trazer uma cobertura ampla do game que marca o retorno da franquia para Vice City, cidade inspirada em Miami. Embora GTA 6 tenha lançamento oficial marcado para 19 de novembro, a maratona começa um dia antes por causa da liberação antecipada do game no Xbox, que segue o fuso horário da Nova Zelândia. A programação também se conecta à cobertura especial de Black Friday do TecMundo, que contará com lives dedicadas a ofertas, descontos e cupons para aproveitar a data. A expectativa em torno de GTA 6 vai muito além da comunidade gamer. Com 13 anos de distância em relação ao lançamento de GTA 5, o novo capítulo da franquia chega cercado de expectativas sobre o tamanho do mundo aberto, a evolução gráfica e as possibilidades de interação com os personagens e o ambiente. Os primeiros números já dão uma dimensão do fenômeno. Segundo estimativas da empresa Sensor Tower, o jogo ultrapassou US$ 1 bilhão em receita com pré-vendas, considerando mais de 10 milhões de cópias reservadas no PlayStation 5 e Xbox Series X|S. Além disso, Sony e Microsoft confirmaram que o título quebrou os recordes históricos de pré-vendas da PlayStation Store e da Microsoft Store. O retorno a Vice City, a ambientação inspirada na Flórida e a história protagonizada por Jason e Lucia também estão entre os principais atrativos. A Rockstar promete um mundo aberto ainda mais detalhado, com novas possibilidades de exploração e liberdade para os jogadores construírem suas próprias experiências. A história também ganha destaque ao trazer uma dupla de protagonistas. A narrativa acompanha Jason Duval e Lucia Caminos, dois assaltantes que exploram o mundo do crime em Vice City após serem inseridos em uma grande conspiração na cidade. Confira 26 minutos de gameplay de GTA 6, que chega em 19 de novembro no PS5 e Xbox Series S/X Olhar Estendido divulgado pela Rockstar Games apresenta detalhes da jogabilidade do aguardado Grand Theft Auto VI. Além da narrativa cinematográfica, o jogo também promete impressionar ao trazer um mundo aberto vivo e repleto de atividades. O jogador poderá roubar carros, assaltar lojas, fazer academia e sair em casal para comprar roupas, fazer a unha e comer em diferentes tipos de estabelecimentos. Apesar da empolgação do público, GTA 6 também chega acompanhado de discussões sobre suas decisões comerciais. No Brasil, a edição Standard custa R$ 449,90, enquanto a Ultimate Edition sai por R$ 549,90 nas lojas digitais oficiais, valores que colocam o lançamento entre os jogos mais caros do mercado nacional. O game também sofreu uma alteração de preço no exterior, sendo um dos primeiros títulos do mundo a adotar o valor padrão de US$ 80 para a edição base e US$ 100 para a versão Ultimate. Segundo Strauss Zelnick, CEO da Take-Two, dona da Rockstar Games, a empresa poderia ter extrapolado esse valor dado o sucesso da franquia. De acordo com o executivo, o preço atual, apesar de alto, é considerado justo pela companhia e atenderá às expectativas dos jogadores. “Nosso trabalho, porém, como vemos, é sempre entregar muito mais valor ao consumidor do que o preço que cobramos”, disse Zelnick, em agosto. Outra questão que chamou a atenção dos jogadores é a comercialização de uma versão física sem disco. Nesse formato, os consumidores recebem um código para baixar o jogo digitalmente, o que gerou críticas de quem esperava uma mídia física tradicional para colecionar ou revender posteriormente. Além das polêmicas que cercam o jogo, a Rockstar Games também está passando por um momento marcante atualmente. Antes do lançamento do game, funcionários da empresa votarão para decidir sobre a abertura de um sindicato de desenvolvedores , o que pode trazer alterações no método de trabalho de futuros projetos da companhia. GTA 6 será lançado para PlayStation 5 e Xbox Series X|S, incluindo os modelos tradicionais e as versões mais potentes dos consoles. Até o momento, a Rockstar Games não anunciou uma data de lançamento para PC. Quem já realizou a compra antecipada do game pode fazer o download do jogo, que pesa mais de 200 GB. Assim, é possível aproveitar o gameplay assim que o título for liberado, a partir do dia 18 de novembro. Em um cenário repleto de expectativas, a transmissão ao vivo do TecMundo e o Voxel visa apresentar cada detalhe da chegada do jogo. A dica é ficar de olho não apenas no YouTube, mas também acompanhar redes sociais e o nosso site, no Estadão, para ficar de olho em todas as notícias, reportagens e vídeos sobre o aguardado game. Essa matéria não é patrocinada, mas contém links de parceiros. O TecMundo pode ganhar comissão pelas vendas geradas por meio desses links. Reiteramos nosso compromisso em indicar apenas produtos e promoções curados e selecionados pelos nossos especialistas, sempre levando em consideração a experiência dos nossos leitores. sources.title: GTA 6 e mais! Veja os lançamentos de games da semana
sources.text: TecMundo fará lives diárias de GTA 6 até a Black Friday! Veja como acompanhar Mais uma semana começa com a nossa lista de lançamentos, para te ajudar a se programar para os próximos dias. O grande destaque desta vez não poderia ser outro além de Grand Theft Auto VI , o novo jogo de mundo aberto da Rockstar Games ambientado em Vice City, que promete ser um dos títulos mais vendidos da história. Outro destaque é Spirit Crossing . O game cooperativo permite que você se junte a outros jogadores para povoar vilas, decorando casas e seus ambientes, em uma jogabilidade divertida e aconchegante. Confira a lista completa de lançamentos da semana e seus preços. Motocross The Game é um simulador de corrida que busca reproduzir a física do esporte sobre duas rodas. No game, a motocicleta e o piloto funcionam como corpos físicos separados, exigindo que o jogador controle a transferência de peso, o acelerador, a embreagem e a inclinação no ar para encarar diferentes tipos de terreno e pistas. O título chega em acesso antecipado para PC e conta com modos para um jogador e partidas multiplayer online em servidores dedicados. Além de permitir personalizar os equipamentos do piloto e os gráficos da moto, o game inclui assistências ajustáveis para iniciantes e rankings globais de contra-relógio. O jogo ainda não tem preço definido no Brasil. Spirit Crossing é um jogo multiplayer online desenvolvido pela Spry Fox, estúdio responsável por títulos como Cozy Grove . Ambientada na região conhecida como Crosslands, a experiência foca na cooperação entre jogadores para construir e decorar tanto casas próprias quanto espaços comunitários compartilhados pelo mapa. Durante a exploração, os jogadores interagem com habitantes locais, incluindo humanos, ursos falantes e espíritos. É preciso ajudá-los a resolver tarefas e acompanhar o desenvolvimento de suas histórias ao longo do tempo. O título aposta em uma abordagem voltada para a convivência e o progresso gradual, sem foco em combate. O game ainda não tem preço definido Depois de 13 anos de espera, GTA 6 será finalmente lançado. O novo jogo de ação e aventura em mundo aberto da Rockstar Games marca o retorno da franquia para o estado de Leonida e as ruas de Vice City. A história acompanha a dupla de protagonistas Lucia Caminos e Jason Duval em uma trama que envolve assaltos, perseguições e atividades criminosas pela região. Além de expandir a escala do mapa e a quantidade de atividades paralelas disponíveis para exploração, o título apresenta melhorias técnicas voltadas para os consoles da atual geração. O jogo já está em pré-venda a partir de R$ 449,90. E na sua opinião, qual o game mais esperado da semana? Conte para a gente nas redes sociais do Voxel!
